invocation_origin: jswarm.portal example fixture (shipped so the UAT/FIX portal has real data to build against on a fresh clone)

evidence_refs.description: Same reproduction log the defect contract cites, confirming the fix removes the early expiry.

decision: Anchor the expiry check to the token's own issued-at claim instead of server receive time.
summary: The session-expiry comparison now uses the token's `issued_at` claim as the anchor, so ordinary clock skew between issuer and host no longer shortens the effective session.

pm_view.quote: A session advertised as lasting an hour now lasts the full hour, every time.

terminal_outcome.statement: A session issued with a given Max-Age lasts that long, regardless of ordinary clock skew between the issuer and the session host.
bullets: Expiry is computed as issued_at + max_age, not received_at + max_age.
A skew of up to 5 seconds between issuer and host no longer shortens the effective session.

pm_anchor_map.controlling_sentence: session_expiry.py now computes expiry = issued_at + max_age instead of received_at + max_age.
pm_anchor_map.how_it_serves: Names the exact line changed, so the repair is traceable to the charted defect.

in_scope.item: Session expiry calculation in the auth middleware.
in_scope.reason: Direct repair of the charted defect.

out_of_scope.reason: Not needed to fix the expiry calculation.

defects.conviction: Confirmed by reproduction: a session with Max-Age=3600 issued at T is rejected as expired at T+3540, consistently, across three independent sessions.
defects.fixed_means: Anchor the expiry comparison to the token's issued_at claim instead of received_at.

flow.body: issue token(issued_at=T, max_age=3600) -> host receives at T+delta -> host computes expiry = issued_at + max_age -> session expires at the advertised time regardless of delta

risks.risk: A host whose clock is skewed far enough backward could accept a token slightly past its true expiry.
risks.impact: Bounded by the existing 5-second skew tolerance already enforced elsewhere in the token verifier.
risks.guardrail: The existing skew-tolerance check is untouched; only the expiry anchor field changes.

cost_timeline.text: Single-file change; verified locally in under a day.

sections.title: The change
sections.body: `session_expiry.py` now reads `token.issued_at` and computes `expiry = issued_at + max_age`, replacing the previous `expiry = received_at + max_age`.

sections.title: Verification
sections.body: Re-ran the fixed-clock-skew reproduction rig from the defect contract; the session that previously expired at T+3540 now expires at T+3600 as advertised.

uat_route: Sign in, wait until shortly before the advertised session lifetime elapses, and confirm the session is still valid at that point.
vendor_policy: No third-party or vendor code is touched by this fix; the expiry calculation is first-party.

authorized_defects.fixed_means: Anchor the expiry comparison to the token's issued_at claim instead of received_at.

implementation_boundaries: Touch only the expiry comparison in the auth middleware's session validation path.

causal_test_obligations.obligation: A session issued with Max-Age=N must remain valid for the full N seconds under a 5-second issuer/host clock skew.

connected_proof.obligation: The fixed-clock-skew reproduction rig must pass against the patched expiry calculation.

counterexamples.description: A session validated with received_at more than 5 seconds behind issued_at must still be rejected as invalid, not silently extended.

rollout.plan: Deploy to the auth middleware service; no data migration or client change is required.

batch_tail_policy.text: This is the only fix in the batch; no tail items remain.

revision_behavior.within_scope: Any within-scope revision (e.g. adjusting the skew tolerance) is auto-included under the existing owner approval.
revision_behavior.scope_widening: Any change that touches token issuance or format returns to the owner before issuance.

must_still_work: A session that is genuinely past its Max-Age is still rejected as expired.
The existing 5-second skew tolerance in the token verifier is unaffected.
